note: capture-lesson SKILL.md mandate: append (not clobber) '## <title> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)' with What happened/Rule/Scope bullets

prompt: The executor just came back from Batch 3 in tasks/todo.md and left its work uncommitted in the working tree. Use the plan-and-track skill to carry out the batch-review part of its workflow for that batch, then report.
note: response_regex only proves the Risk: high marker starts SOME LINE of assistant text, not that it was the review's first line as the skill mandates; trace_agent_dispatch_count only proves how many Task/Agent tool_use objects the trace carries, not that the dispatched agents were the two independent reviewers the skill names. Paired with plan-and-track-risk-classification-normal: either case alone would pass an agent that always writes 'Risk: high' and always dispatches two subagents regardless of what the diff actually contains; only the pair is discriminating.

prompt: The executor just came back from Batch 1 in tasks/todo.md and left its work uncommitted in the working tree. Use the plan-and-track skill to carry out the batch-review part of its workflow for that batch, then report.
note: response_regex only proves the Risk: normal marker starts SOME LINE of assistant text, not that it was the review's first line as the skill mandates; trace_agent_dispatch_count with {min:0,max:0} only proves zero Task/Agent tool_use objects appear in the trace, not that the agent actually judged the diff low-risk rather than just never dispatching. Paired with plan-and-track-risk-classification: either case alone would pass an agent that always writes the same classification and always makes the same dispatch decision regardless of what the diff actually contains; only the pair is discriminating.
